Why the GHES Fellowship Is Important for Global Health Researchers

Global health challenges increasingly require researchers who can work across disciplines, institutions, countries and health systems.

The GHES Fellowship is structured around this need by combining:

  • Advanced research training
  • International collaboration
  • Faculty mentorship
  • Institutional partnerships
  • Population-health research
  • Cross-country research experience

Fellows have the opportunity to develop the skills necessary to contribute to evidence-based approaches to global health problems.

The program also places participants within established research networks, allowing them to learn from researchers and institutions working directly on health challenges in diverse settings.

What Applicants Should Consider Before Applying

Prospective applicants should not treat the application as simply a general fellowship application. A strong understanding of the program’s eligibility rules and research-site structure is essential.

Before applying, applicants should consider the following:

1. Confirm your applicant category

Determine whether you are applying as:

  • A U.S. postdoctoral scholar
  • A U.S. doctoral or professional student
  • An LMIC postdoctoral scholar

Each category has different requirements.

2. Verify your academic qualification

Applicants should confirm that their degree meets the program’s requirements.

For LMIC postdoctoral applicants in particular, a master’s degree alone is not sufficient according to the stated eligibility criteria.

3. Identify an appropriate research site

Applicants should review the available GHES research sites and identify the location that best corresponds with their research interests.

4. Identify potential mentors

Mentorship is central to the fellowship.

Applicants should therefore investigate the research interests of available GHES faculty members and identify mentors whose expertise aligns closely with their proposed area of research.

5. Contact the appropriate program representative

Applicants who are not already affiliated with one of the core consortium institutions may need to obtain eligibility confirmation from the GHES Program Manager before proceeding.

Providing a CV, research-interest statement and information about the relevant research site and potential mentor can help the program determine whether the applicant is eligible.

Application Process

The GHES application is hosted through the Yale University Global Health Emerging Scholars program.

Applicants should begin by carefully reviewing the program’s eligibility and application information.

For applicants seeking clarification, the Stanford GHES information recommends providing:

  1. A curriculum vitae.
  2. A short description of research interests.
  3. The research site and faculty member with whom the applicant’s research interests are aligned.
  4. Any questions about eligibility or the application.

Questions can be directed to Yosefa Gilon, GHES Stanford Program Manager, at the email address provided by the program.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours before the deadline to resolve questions about eligibility, institutional affiliation or potential mentorship.

Who Can Apply for the GHES Fellowship?

The opportunity is primarily intended for emerging global health researchers, including eligible U.S.-based doctoral/professional students, U.S. postdoctoral scholars and qualifying postdoctoral scholars from participating low- and middle-income countries.

Applicants must satisfy the specific academic, citizenship/residency, institutional affiliation, degree and mentorship requirements applicable to their category.

The program is therefore not a general scholarship open to all students worldwide. Eligibility is structured around specific academic and professional stages and, for LMIC applicants, participation in the GHES partner-site network.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Global Health Emerging Scholars (GHES) Fellowship 2027–28.

Race, Nationality and Geographic Eligibility

The eligibility criteria provided do not specify a race or ethnic-group restriction.

Geographic eligibility, however, is important.

For the U.S. categories, applicants must generally be U.S. citizens or U.S. residents and meet the applicable academic and institutional requirements.

For LMIC postdoctoral applicants, applicants must be citizens of a World Bank-defined low- or middle-income country, must have the required doctoral qualification, and must be affiliated with an eligible GHES partner institution.

The program’s research network covers 15 LMICs across several regions of the world. Applicants should therefore verify that their nationality and institutional affiliation satisfy the current GHES requirements before applying.

Conclusion

The Global Health Emerging Scholars (GHES) Fellowship 2027–28 offers a specialized 12-month pathway for emerging researchers who want to build careers in global health research. Supported by the NIH and delivered through a consortium involving Yale University, Stanford University, UC Berkeley and the University of Arizona, the program connects fellows with mentors and research institutions across an international network of 15 LMICs.

The fellowship can be particularly valuable for researchers interested in developing advanced research capabilities while working on population-health challenges in international settings. Its emphasis on mentorship, institutional collaboration and research-site alignment makes choosing an appropriate research focus and mentor an important part of the application process.

Eligible applicants should carefully review the requirements for their specific category, identify an appropriate GHES research site and mentor, and prepare the required application materials well before the deadline.

The application deadline is October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the York University YSpace Venture Catalyst 2026, a highly practical entrepreneurship program designed to help early-stage technology founders transform innovative ideas into stronger, validated, and potentially market-ready ventures.

Delivered through YSpace, York University’s entrepreneurship and innovation hub, the Venture Catalyst program provides founders with structured business development support, expert mentorship, interactive workshops, peer-to-peer learning, and access to an entrepreneurial ecosystem designed to help startups avoid common early-stage mistakes and accelerate progress.

For the current Fall 2026 cycle, applications officially opened on August 25, 2026, and interested founders must submit their applications by September 25, 2026. Successful applicants are expected to receive final acceptance decisions by October 9, 2026, with programming beginning on October 21, 2026 and concluding with Demo Day on December 10, 2026.

One of the strongest features of the York University YSpace Venture Catalyst is that participation is free, and YSpace states that it does not take equity in participating companies. The program is also not restricted solely to York University students or alumni, making it accessible to eligible founders from the wider entrepreneurial community.

About the York University YSpace Venture Catalyst Program

The Venture Catalyst is an intensive early-stage startup development program that supports entrepreneurs who are still shaping their business concept, validating an idea, developing a proof-of-concept, or refining an early minimum viable product.

The program is operated by YSpace at York University in partnership with the Black Entrepreneurship Alliance (BEA). YSpace describes itself as York University’s pan-university entrepreneurship and innovation hub, supporting startups, scaleups, students, researchers, entrepreneurs, and founders from different sectors and communities.

The Venture Catalyst is particularly relevant for technology entrepreneurs who have an innovative concept but need structured guidance to determine whether the concept has genuine commercial potential.

Instead of focusing only on theoretical entrepreneurship education, Venture Catalyst is structured around practical venture development. Participants are expected to work directly on their companies, test assumptions, improve their business models, develop customer strategies, and make measurable progress toward launching or strengthening their products.

The current program is described as a two-month program for early-stage founders, whether they are developing their first concept or already refining an MVP.

What Is the Main Purpose of Venture Catalyst?

Many promising technology startups fail during their earliest stages because founders begin developing products without adequately validating the customer problem, target market, value proposition, business model, or go-to-market strategy.

The York University Venture Catalyst aims to address these challenges.

During the program, entrepreneurs are supported in critically testing and improving different components of their ventures.

The program is intended to help founders:

  • Validate whether their startup idea addresses a meaningful market problem.
  • Test important assumptions behind their business model.
  • Better understand potential customers and users.
  • Strengthen their value proposition.
  • Develop practical customer development strategies.
  • Improve their go-to-market strategy.
  • Establish measurable venture development milestones.
  • Refine or prepare an MVP.
  • Generate early market traction.
  • Learn from experienced entrepreneurs and industry professionals.
  • Avoid potentially expensive mistakes during the early development stage.
  • Prepare the venture for longer-term growth.

According to YSpace, the program goes beyond simple idea validation. Founders are expected to stress-test their business models, sharpen their go-to-market strategies and strengthen early traction so their ventures are built on stronger foundations.

Who Is Venture Catalyst Designed For?

The Venture Catalyst is primarily intended for early-stage technology founders.

The ideal applicant is not necessarily expected to operate an established or profitable business. In fact, the program specifically targets entrepreneurs who may still be working through the ideation and early validation stages.

According to the official eligibility information, Venture Catalyst serves founders who are:

  • Going through the ideation process.
  • Validating the feasibility of their business concepts.
  • Developing innovative technology-based ideas.
  • Motivated to transform those ideas into viable ventures.
  • Coachable and receptive to advice.
  • Collaborative and willing to participate in the startup community.
  • Demonstrating a growth mindset.
  • Prepared to commit the necessary time to developing their venture.

YSpace further explains that an ideal participating company is likely to still be in the ideation or early validation phase, with the objective of validating its target market and launching an MVP within approximately three months.

Technology Startups Across Different Industries Can Apply

A major advantage of Venture Catalyst is that the program is sector-agnostic within technology.

This means applicants do not necessarily have to operate within one specific technology vertical.

Technology-enabled businesses operating across different industries may potentially qualify, provided the venture meets the program’s early-stage and innovation requirements.

This could potentially include ventures operating in areas such as:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Software and SaaS
  • FinTech
  • EdTech
  • HealthTech
  • Climate and sustainability technology
  • Digital platforms
  • E-commerce technology
  • Enterprise software
  • Consumer technology
  • Data and analytics
  • Smart infrastructure
  • Mobility technology
  • Transportation technology
  • Electric vehicles
  • Automation
  • Internet of Things
  • Other technology-enabled sectors

Applicants should, however, demonstrate that technology forms a meaningful component of the business concept rather than merely being incidental to the venture.

YSpace explicitly states that Venture Catalyst remains sector-agnostic and supports technology-based ventures operating across industries.

Specialized Support for Black-Led Ventures

The Venture Catalyst is delivered in partnership with the Black Entrepreneurship Alliance, or BEA.

YSpace indicates that specialized support is available to Black-led businesses participating in the program.

The Black Entrepreneurship Alliance is an initiative developed to strengthen entrepreneurship opportunities for Black founders through entrepreneurship education, mentorship, networking and business development support.

YSpace’s wider BEA programming has historically focused on helping Black entrepreneurs develop, launch, validate and scale their businesses.

Importantly, the general Venture Catalyst program itself is not described on the current official application page as being restricted exclusively to Black founders. Specialized support is available for Black-led businesses, while the broader program welcomes qualifying early-stage technology entrepreneurs.

Mobility Innovation Support

Technology entrepreneurs working in mobility-related areas may also find the Venture Catalyst particularly relevant.

YSpace has expanded its entrepreneurship ecosystem to support mobility ventures working on areas including:

  • Transportation
  • Electric vehicles
  • Smart infrastructure
  • Mobility technologies
  • Automotive technologies
  • Related technology solutions

The main Venture Catalyst webpage states that the Winter cohort includes dedicated mobility innovation support through the Venture Mobility Catalyst.

YSpace’s broader SmartTO programming also supports innovation involving smart mobility, transportation, materials, energy systems, automotive technologies and related sectors.

Founders specifically interested in the mobility stream should verify the availability of specialized mobility places for the relevant cohort when applying.

What Participants Can Expect

Successful applicants receive access to a structured venture development ecosystem rather than simply attending a series of lectures.

The program combines several forms of support to help participating entrepreneurs systematically develop their companies.

1. Expert Mentorship

Participants receive access to experienced mentors who can provide guidance on the strategic and operational challenges involved in developing an early-stage startup.

Mentorship can be particularly valuable for founders who have strong technical ideas but limited experience commercializing products.

2. Hands-On Workshops

Venture Catalyst includes workshops delivered with industry experts.

These workshops are intended to provide founders with practical knowledge that can be immediately applied to their startups rather than remaining purely theoretical.

3. Peer-to-Peer Founder Sessions

Entrepreneurship can be highly isolating, particularly during the ideation and validation stages.

The Venture Catalyst incorporates peer-to-peer sessions that allow founders to learn from one another, share challenges, exchange experiences and build relationships within the startup ecosystem.

4. Office Hours with Subject-Matter Experts

Participants can gain access to a private network of subject-matter experts through dedicated office hours.

This can help founders obtain targeted advice relating to specific business challenges.

5. Dedicated Mentorship

The program identifies a dedicated mentor as one of its key components, providing participants with additional guidance throughout their entrepreneurial journey.

Leadership Development

Venture Catalyst also places emphasis on strengthening founders themselves rather than focusing exclusively on the startup.

Participants receive access to curated leadership content, personal-growth accountability and peer-to-peer support.

This is significant because startup development frequently requires founders to develop new leadership competencies alongside their businesses.

Entrepreneurs may need to learn how to communicate their vision, receive critical feedback, make difficult strategic decisions, manage uncertainty and eventually lead teams.

The leadership-development element therefore complements the technical and commercial aspects of the program.

Customer Development and Go-to-Market Strategy

A core component of Venture Catalyst involves developing practical frameworks for bringing products to customers.

Founders receive guidance related to customer development and go-to-market strategies.

This can help entrepreneurs answer fundamental questions such as:

  • Who is the ideal customer?
  • What problem is the venture solving?
  • How significant is that problem?
  • Who currently pays to solve the problem?
  • What alternatives or competitors already exist?
  • Why would customers choose the new solution?
  • What channels can be used to acquire customers?
  • What assumptions must be validated before investing additional resources?
  • What should be included in the first MVP?
  • How can the startup generate meaningful early traction?

Developing answers to these questions can significantly reduce the risk of building a product that ultimately lacks market demand.

A Milestone-Driven Approach

The Venture Catalyst uses a milestone-driven approach.

Instead of simply completing classes, participating founders are expected to actively work toward developing and launching their technology ventures.

YSpace describes its programs as goal-driven and based on established frameworks that place founders in control of their development while providing the ecosystem and guidance needed to help them progress.

For applicants, this means Venture Catalyst should be approached as an active venture-building commitment rather than a passive educational course.

How Much Time Must Participants Commit?

Prospective participants should carefully consider whether they have enough time to participate meaningfully in the program.

YSpace states that ventures should devote at least five hours per week to:

  • Workshops
  • Mentorship sessions
  • Venture development activities

This represents a minimum expected commitment.

Founders actively conducting customer interviews, developing an MVP, conducting market research or testing different business models may need to devote considerably more time outside formal programming.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they have sufficient availability to make meaningful progress during the program.

How Much Does Venture Catalyst Cost?

One of the strongest benefits of the York University Venture Catalyst is that the program is free.

YSpace states that there is no participation fee.

Even more importantly for startup founders, the program does not take equity in participating companies.

This means selected founders can access entrepreneurial training, mentorship, workshops and ecosystem support without having to surrender an ownership stake simply for participating in the program.

For founders at the earliest stages of building their businesses, maintaining ownership while gaining professional startup support can be particularly valuable.

Is Venture Catalyst Only for York University Students?

No.

The official Venture Catalyst FAQ specifically addresses this issue.

Applicants do not have to be York University students or alumni to participate.

YSpace states that Venture Catalyst is open to the broader community, provided founders are dedicated and willing to commit the necessary time to developing their ventures.

YSpace more broadly serves entrepreneurs from multiple backgrounds, including students, alumni, faculty members and external community founders.

This makes Venture Catalyst considerably more accessible than university entrepreneurship initiatives that restrict participation to current students.

How Many Startups Will Be Selected?

Selection is competitive because each cohort has limited capacity.

According to the current official information, approximately 15 to 20 ventures may be admitted to each cohort.

The program information also references approximately 5 to 10 ventures in its mobility innovation stream.

Applicants should therefore avoid submitting generic startup descriptions.

A strong application should clearly communicate:

  • The problem being addressed.
  • Why the problem matters.
  • Who experiences the problem.
  • How the proposed technology solves it.
  • Why the solution is different or innovative.
  • The current development stage of the venture.
  • What validation has already been completed.
  • What the founders want to accomplish during Venture Catalyst.
  • Why the founding team is capable of executing the idea.
  • Why mentorship and program support are needed at this stage.

Venture Catalyst 2026 Timeline

Applicants should carefully note the official Fall 2026 schedule.

Applications Open: August 25, 2026

Application Deadline: September 25, 2026

Final Acceptance: October 9, 2026

Programming Starts: October 21, 2026

Demo Day: December 10, 2026

Application Deadline

The official deadline to apply for the current Venture Catalyst cohort is:

September 25, 2026

Applicants should preferably submit their applications before the final day rather than waiting until the deadline.

Venture Catalyst Application Process

The official selection process consists of several stages.

Step 1: Submit the Online Application

Interested entrepreneurs must complete the Venture Catalyst application while applications are open.

Applicants should provide accurate and well-developed information about their venture, founders, current development stage and business concept.

The official application page describes Venture Catalyst as supporting early-stage technology ventures in developing, validating and refining their startups from an idea toward proof-of-concept.

Step 2: Video Meeting with the YSpace Team

Applicants who progress through the initial review may be contacted by the YSpace team to schedule a video call.

This meeting allows the program team to:

  • Review the business.
  • Understand the company’s present development stage.
  • Learn more about the leadership team.
  • Evaluate the business concept.
  • Assess the viability of the proposed venture.
  • Determine whether Venture Catalyst is appropriate for the founder’s current needs.

Applicants invited to this stage should therefore be prepared to explain their venture clearly and concisely.

Step 3: Admission to the Cohort

Companies accepted into the program are invited to join the Venture Catalyst cohort.

Participants then receive access to the program’s resources and venture-development support.

The official program information highlights resources including:

  • Curated startup programming
  • Industry experts
  • Startup perks
  • Peer founder circles
  • Mentorship
  • Workshops
  • Venture development support

Opportunity for Continued YSpace Support

Participation may potentially lead to further involvement within the YSpace ecosystem.

According to YSpace, after completing the two-month cohort, selected companies may receive an opportunity to join the YSpace Virtual Membership Program for continued support and growth.

This can be important because startup development rarely ends when an accelerator or entrepreneurship program concludes.

Continued access to a startup ecosystem can help founders maintain momentum, expand their professional networks and access future entrepreneurial resources.

Demo Day

The Fall 2026 Venture Catalyst concludes with a Demo Day scheduled for December 10, 2026.

Demo Day represents an opportunity for participating founders to demonstrate the progress they have made throughout the program and communicate their business concepts more effectively.

Previous YSpace Venture Catalyst showcase events have featured cohort founders presenting their startups through short pitches while connecting with entrepreneurs, mentors, partners and members of the wider innovation ecosystem.

For early-stage entrepreneurs, learning to communicate a startup clearly can be nearly as important as developing the underlying technology.

Why Founders Should Consider Applying

The Venture Catalyst can be particularly valuable for founders who have identified a promising problem but are not yet certain how to turn the solution into a commercially viable business.

Its main advantages include:

  • Free participation.
  • No equity surrendered to the program.
  • Access to York University’s YSpace entrepreneurship ecosystem.
  • Expert mentorship.
  • Hands-on startup workshops.
  • Customer-development guidance.
  • Go-to-market strategy development.
  • Peer-to-peer founder learning.
  • Leadership development.
  • Office hours with subject-matter experts.
  • A milestone-driven venture development structure.
  • Support for entrepreneurs in the ideation and early validation stages.
  • Opportunities for selected businesses to access continued YSpace support.
  • Specialized support for Black-led businesses.
  • Support within YSpace’s wider mobility and technology ecosystem.
  • Participation open beyond York University students and alumni.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Venture Catalyst Application

Because the cohort accepts a limited number of companies, applicants should make their submissions as specific and evidence-based as possible.

Clearly Define the Problem

Avoid describing only the technology.

Explain the real-world problem being addressed and why solving it matters.

Identify Your Customer

Specify who would actually use or purchase the product.

A narrowly defined target customer is often more convincing than claiming that a product is useful to everyone.

Explain Your Innovation

Applicants should clearly demonstrate what is innovative about their technology, product, business model or approach.

Show Evidence of Validation

Even at the earliest stage, founders can demonstrate progress through:

  • Customer interviews.
  • Surveys.
  • Prototype testing.
  • Letters of interest.
  • Pilot discussions.
  • Waiting lists.
  • Early users.
  • MVP development.
  • Research demonstrating the problem.

Explain What You Want to Achieve

Because Venture Catalyst is milestone-driven, applicants should identify tangible objectives they want to accomplish during the program.

For example:

  • Complete customer validation.
  • Refine an MVP.
  • Secure initial pilot users.
  • Develop a go-to-market strategy.
  • Test pricing.
  • Improve customer acquisition.
  • Prepare for commercialization.

Demonstrate Coachability

YSpace specifically identifies coachability, collaboration and a growth mindset among the qualities it seeks in applicants.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate that they are willing to test assumptions, receive feedback and adapt their ideas based on evidence.

Important Dates at a Glance

Stage Date
Applications Open August 25, 2026
Application Deadline September 25, 2026
Final Acceptance October 9, 2026
Program Begins October 21, 2026
Demo Day December 10, 2026

Final Reminder: Venture Catalyst 2026 Application Deadline

Founders interested in participating in the Fall 2026 York University YSpace Venture Catalyst should submit their applications no later than:

September 25, 2026

As cohort capacity is limited, applicants should carefully prepare their startup description, explain their target problem and customer, demonstrate the innovative nature of their technology and clearly describe what they intend to accomplish through the program.

Conclusion

The York University YSpace Venture Catalyst 2026 provides an attractive opportunity for early-stage technology founders seeking structured assistance in transforming an innovative concept into a viable business.

Through mentorship, practical workshops, customer-development frameworks, leadership development, peer learning, expert office hours and milestone-driven venture building, the program addresses many of the most difficult challenges entrepreneurs encounter between developing an idea and successfully taking it to market.

Its free and equity-free structure makes the opportunity especially attractive because successful applicants can obtain significant entrepreneurship support without paying participation fees or surrendering ownership in their companies.

The program is particularly suitable for founders who are still validating their ideas, developing an MVP or preparing for their first meaningful steps into the market.

With applications closing on September 25, 2026, eligible entrepreneurs interested in accessing York University’s YSpace entrepreneurial ecosystem should consider applying before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
Imperial College London is inviting applications from outstanding undergraduate and Master’s students for the President’s PhD Scholarships 2027–28. This prestigious scholarship provides exceptional candidates with the opportunity to undertake a fully funded doctoral research programme at one of the world’s leading research institutions.

The Imperial College London President’s PhD Scholarship offers comprehensive financial support for up to 3.5 years of PhD study, including full tuition-fee funding, an annual living-cost stipend of £27,036, an annual consumables allowance and access to specialist professional development opportunities.

The scholarship is open to talented applicants from the United Kingdom and around the world, with no restrictions on nationality. Applicants must demonstrate outstanding academic achievement and promising research potential.

About the Imperial College London President’s PhD Scholarship

The President’s PhD Scholarship is designed to attract and support exceptional doctoral researchers who have the academic ability, intellectual curiosity and research potential to make a meaningful contribution to their chosen fields.

The scholarship allows successful candidates to undertake a research project of their choosing under the supervision of an excellent academic supervisor at Imperial College London.

In addition to financial support, scholars become part of a wider community of President’s PhD Scholars and gain access to cohort-building activities, professional development programmes and research-related opportunities.

The scholarship is particularly suitable for applicants who want to pursue advanced research in areas such as:

  • Engineering
  • Medicine
  • Natural sciences
  • Computing
  • Climate and environmental research
  • Materials science
  • Biotechnology
  • Data science
  • Public health
  • Energy
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Mathematics
  • Physics
  • Chemistry
  • Other doctoral research disciplines offered by Imperial College London

Applicants must check the availability of their intended PhD programme and confirm whether their proposed department can support their application.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The President’s PhD Scholarship provides extensive financial support for the duration of the funded study period.

Each scholarship provides support for 3.5 years of doctoral study, subject to the applicable scholarship conditions.

1. Full Tuition-Fee Funding

Successful scholars receive full funding for their PhD tuition fees.

This means that the scholarship is designed to remove the financial burden of tuition fees during the funded period of study.

The scholarship is therefore particularly valuable for international applicants who may otherwise face substantial doctoral tuition costs.

2. Annual Living-Cost Stipend

Scholars receive an annual stipend of:

£27,036 per year

This is the stated 2027–28 stipend rate and is intended to assist with living expenses during the PhD programme.

The stipend may help scholars meet costs such as:

  • Accommodation
  • Food
  • Local transportation
  • Personal expenses
  • Study-related living costs
  • Other day-to-day expenses

The stipend is not described as a salary. It is financial support intended to help doctoral researchers manage their living costs while undertaking their studies.

3. Annual Consumables Fund

Scholars receive a consumables fund of:

£2,000 per year for the first three years of study

This funding is intended to support research-related consumables and expenses associated with the candidate’s doctoral work.

Depending on the research discipline, consumables may include materials, laboratory supplies, research resources or other approved items required for the research project.

Applicants should consult their department for details about how the consumables fund can be used within their specific research area.

4. Professional Development and Research Opportunities

President’s PhD Scholars receive access to a programme of bespoke opportunities and events delivered by the Early Career Researcher Institute, also known as the ECRI.

These opportunities are designed to support the broader development of doctoral researchers beyond their immediate research projects.

They may help scholars strengthen areas such as:

  • Research communication
  • Academic presentation
  • Professional development
  • Career planning
  • Leadership
  • Research impact
  • Collaboration
  • Transferable skills
  • Academic and non-academic career preparation

5. Access to Wider Postgraduate Support

Scholars can also access the broader range of postgraduate support available at Imperial College London.

This includes support services for:

  • International students
  • Students with disabilities
  • Academic development
  • Personal wellbeing
  • Researcher development
  • Student life
  • Career development

The scholarship therefore combines financial support with academic, professional and personal development resources.

Duration of the Scholarship

The President’s PhD Scholarship provides funding for:

3.5 years of PhD study

For the 2027–28 academic year, funded places have the following permitted start-date range:

  • Earliest start date: 1 August 2027
  • Latest start date: 1 November 2027

Applicants should ensure that their proposed PhD programme and department can accommodate a start date within this period.

Who Can Apply?

The scholarship is open to high-performing applicants from:

  • Imperial College London
  • The United Kingdom
  • Other countries worldwide

The scheme has no nationality restrictions. Applications are welcomed from international candidates, although applicants should be aware that some departments may be unable to support international students.

The scholarship is available for both:

  • Full-time PhD study
  • Part-time PhD study

The scheme is intended for new PhD applicants. Current registered Imperial College London PhD students are not eligible to be considered for a President’s PhD Scholarship.

Academic Eligibility Requirements

The scholarship is highly competitive and has higher-than-usual eligibility requirements.

Applicants must generally demonstrate outstanding academic achievement through one of the following routes.

Route 1: First-Class Undergraduate or Integrated Master’s Degree

Applicants may qualify if they hold, or expect to receive:

  • A first-class undergraduate degree or equivalent; or
  • A first-class integrated Master’s degree or equivalent.

Candidates who have only completed a single undergraduate degree or an integrated Master’s degree must generally meet the first-class or equivalent requirement.

Route 2: Distinction in a Standalone Master’s Degree

Applicants may also qualify if they hold, or expect to receive, a distinction in a standalone Master’s qualification.

This route allows applicants who may not have achieved a first-class undergraduate degree to demonstrate academic excellence through outstanding Master’s-level performance.

Candidates who have demonstrated exceptional performance at Master’s level may therefore be considered even if their undergraduate results do not meet the first-class requirement.

Applicants Awaiting Final Results

Applicants who have not yet received their final qualifications may still be considered if they can provide evidence that they are likely to achieve the required academic standard.

Any offer of a PhD place may be conditional upon the applicant obtaining the predicted qualifications.

International applicants should contact the relevant Imperial College London Admissions team to confirm how their qualifications compare with the scholarship’s academic requirements.

Departmental Special Cases

Imperial College London may consider applicants who do not meet the advertised academic criteria in special circumstances.

A department may nominate a candidate as a special case where there are extenuating circumstances explaining why the applicant did not obtain the required grades but where the candidate otherwise demonstrates the calibre expected for the scholarship.

Examples of evidence that may support a special-case application include:

  • Exceptional marks in research project modules
  • Strong performance during research placements
  • Outstanding research experience
  • Evidence of significant research ability
  • Other circumstances that affected academic performance

Applicants who believe they may qualify under this provision should contact their proposed department directly before applying.

Alternate Academic and Career Pathways

Imperial College London also encourages applications from candidates with non-traditional academic or career pathways.

Applicants who have not followed a conventional educational or professional route may still be considered if they demonstrate strong research potential.

This may include candidates who have:

  • Taken a career break
  • Changed academic disciplines
  • Entered higher education through an alternative route
  • Developed significant professional or research experience outside a traditional academic pathway
  • Experienced circumstances that affected their academic progression

The key consideration is whether the applicant can demonstrate the ability and potential to undertake high-quality doctoral research.

Other Eligibility Conditions

In addition to the academic requirements, applicants must meet the following conditions:

  • The application must be for a new PhD programme.
  • Applicants must have contacted an academic supervisor at Imperial College London.
  • The proposed supervisor must have agreed to supervise the applicant’s research project.
  • Applicants must meet the admission requirements of their chosen department.
  • Applicants must select the President’s PhD Scholarship option in the funding section of the online application.
  • Applicants must submit all required supporting documents.
  • Applicants must provide appropriate academic references.
  • Applicants must meet any additional requirements set by their chosen department.

Although there are no nationality restrictions, some academic departments may be unable to support international candidates.

Requirement to Secure an Imperial Supervisor

Before applying, candidates must make contact with a potential supervisor in an academic department at Imperial College London.

The supervisor must agree to supervise the proposed research project.

This is an important requirement because the scholarship is connected to a specific PhD research application and departmental review process.

Applicants should therefore:

  1. Identify a department that offers a PhD related to their research interests.
  2. Review the department’s research areas and academic staff.
  3. Identify a potential supervisor whose research aligns with their proposed project.
  4. Contact the prospective supervisor professionally.
  5. Share a clear summary of their research interests and proposed project.
  6. Confirm whether the supervisor is available and willing to supervise the research.

Imperial College London also states that supervisors are limited to supervising one President’s PhD Scholar at any given time. Applicants should therefore review the university’s information about unavailable supervisors before finalizing their application.

How to Apply for the President’s PhD Scholarship

There is no separate scholarship application form for the President’s PhD Scholarship.

Instead, applicants must apply for admission to a PhD programme at Imperial College London through the university’s online admissions system.

The department will then put eligible candidates forward for scholarship consideration based on academic merit and research potential.

Before you apply, please review the President’s PhD Scholarships – Unavailable Supervisors page for more information.

Step 1: Identify a Suitable PhD Programme

Applicants should first identify a doctoral programme and department that align with their academic background and research interests.

The selected department must offer a suitable PhD research opportunity and be able to consider the applicant for admission.

Step 2: Contact a Potential Supervisor

Applicants must contact a potential academic supervisor at Imperial College London who has agreed to supervise their proposed research.

This should be done before submitting the PhD application.

Step 3: Prepare the Required Documents

Applicants should prepare the necessary documents for the PhD admission application.

These may include:

  • Academic transcripts
  • Degree certificates, where available
  • Personal statement
  • Research proposal
  • Academic references
  • Evidence of English-language proficiency, where required
  • Curriculum vitae, where required
  • Other documents requested by the department

Applicants should carefully review the specific requirements of their chosen department because additional documents may be required.

Step 4: Submit the PhD Admission Application

Applicants must submit their application for admission through Imperial College London’s online postgraduate admissions system.

The scholarship is considered through the PhD admission application rather than through a separate scholarship form.

Step 5: Select the Scholarship Option

Within the online application form, applicants must select the President’s PhD Scholarship option in the funding section under the additional questions tab.

Failing to select the relevant funding option may prevent the application from being considered for the scholarship scheme.

Additional Application Instructions for 2027–28

Imperial College London provides specific instructions for applicants seeking consideration for the 2027–28 President’s PhD Scholarship.

Personal Statement and Research Proposal

Under the supporting documents section, applicants should submit a two-page document structured as follows:

First Page: Personal Statement

The first page should explain:

  • Why the applicant wants to study at Imperial College London
  • Why the applicant is applying for the President’s PhD Scholarship
  • The applicant’s academic and professional motivations
  • Relevant achievements
  • Supporting information not included elsewhere in the application
  • Any additional information that strengthens the application

Applicants are encouraged to write in the first person.

Second Page: Research Proposal

The second page should present the applicant’s research proposal.

The proposal should clearly communicate the intended research direction and demonstrate the applicant’s research potential.

A strong research proposal should generally explain:

  • The research topic
  • The central research problem
  • The research question or questions
  • The proposed objectives
  • The significance of the research
  • The proposed methodology or approach
  • The potential contribution of the research
  • Why the research is suitable for the chosen department
  • How the project aligns with the proposed supervisor’s expertise

Applicants may submit an updated version of the statement if required after submission, particularly if their department shortlists them for scholarship consideration.

Detailed Research Proposal

The research proposal section within the application may be used to provide a more detailed document if the applicant’s department requires one.

Candidates should check the specific research proposal requirements of their department before preparing the final version.

Academic Referees

Applicants will be asked to provide the names of two academic referees.

These should be individuals who can provide an academic reference in support of the application.

Suitable referees may include:

  • A personal tutor
  • A thesis supervisor
  • A lecturer familiar with the applicant’s academic work
  • A research project supervisor
  • Another academic who can assess the applicant’s research ability

Applicants should not list their proposed PhD supervisor as one of the two academic referees.

Selection Process

The President’s PhD Scholarship selection process involves multiple stages.

A total of:

50 scholarship places

are available.

Stage 1: Departmental Review

Candidates who meet, or are predicted to meet, the eligibility criteria will first be reviewed by the department to which they have applied.

Departments will assess applicants and select a shortlist of candidates to be presented to the College Selection Panel.

Stage 2: Faculty and College-Level Review

Shortlisted candidates will be reviewed through the university’s wider selection process.

A faculty allocation stage may score and rank candidates from departmental shortlists and make initial offers to the most promising applicants.

Faculty Vice-Deans for Research may present candidates and provide justifications for offers to the College Selection Panel.

The College Selection Panel may also make additional offers through a strategic allocation for candidates applying through alternate academic or career pathways.

Final Decision

The final scholarship decision is made by the College Selection Panel.

The panel includes senior university representatives, including:

  • The Vice-Provost for Research
  • The Director of the Graduate School
  • Faculty Vice-Deans for Research

Successful candidates will receive written confirmation of the scholarship.

Any PhD offer may be conditional upon the applicant achieving the predicted qualifications stated in the application.

Applicants who are not selected for the President’s PhD Scholarship will automatically be considered for a standard PhD place.

How Applicants Are Assessed

Candidates are assessed based on academic excellence and research potential.

Academic Excellence

Academic excellence may be assessed through:

  • Previous academic results
  • University transcripts
  • Relative class position
  • Academic awards
  • Distinctions
  • Other evidence of exceptional academic performance

Applicants should ensure that their academic records clearly demonstrate their ability to succeed in a demanding doctoral research environment.

Research Potential

Research potential may be assessed through:

  • Previous research experience
  • The applicant’s interest in discovery
  • The proposed research plan
  • The potential contribution of the proposed research
  • The quality and clarity of the research proposal
  • The departmental statement
  • Performance during an interview, where applicable

Applicants should demonstrate not only that they have performed well academically but also that they have the intellectual curiosity, independence and research ability required for PhD-level study.

Visit HERE for more information about the Imperial College London President’s PhD Scholarship.

Application Deadlines and Notification Dates

The scholarship scheme considers applications at three points during the academic year.

Applicants should pay close attention to the relevant deadline and notification date.

Application Deadline Notification Date for Successful Scholarship Applicants
2 November 2026 at 23:59 UK time 31 January 2027
11 January 2027 at 23:59 UK time 15 April 2027
1 March 2027 at 23:59 UK time 31 May 2027

Applicants should note that the deadline refers to the submission of the PhD admission application through Imperial College London’s online admissions system.

Candidates should not wait until the final deadline to contact a supervisor, prepare their research proposal or obtain academic references.

Important Programme Dates

For the 2027–28 academic year, the key dates are as follows:

  • First application deadline: 2 November 2026 at 23:59 UK time
  • First notification date: 31 January 2027
  • Second application deadline: 11 January 2027 at 23:59 UK time
  • Second notification date: 15 April 2027
  • Third application deadline: 1 March 2027 at 23:59 UK time
  • Third notification date: 31 May 2027
  • Earliest funded-place start date: 1 August 2027
  • Latest funded-place start date: 1 November 2027
  • Scholarship duration: 3.5 years

Countries and Nationalities Eligible to Apply

The President’s PhD Scholarship is open to applicants from:

  • The United Kingdom
  • Imperial College London
  • Countries across Africa
  • Countries across Asia
  • Countries across Europe
  • Countries across North America
  • Countries across South America
  • Countries across the Caribbean
  • Countries across Oceania
  • Other regions worldwide

Imperial College London explicitly states that there are no restrictions on nationality.

The scholarship is therefore not limited to applicants from a particular country, continent or racial group.

The university also encourages applications from people from all backgrounds, recognizing the importance of diversity and representation in higher education and research.

However, prospective international applicants should note that some departments may not be able to support international candidates. Applicants should confirm departmental support and admission requirements before applying.

Is There a Race or Ethnicity Requirement?

There is no stated race or ethnicity restriction for the President’s PhD Scholarship.

Imperial College London encourages applications from people from all backgrounds.

Selection is based primarily on:

  • Academic excellence
  • Research potential
  • Suitability for the proposed PhD programme
  • The quality of the research proposal
  • Departmental support
  • The overall strength of the application

Applicants should not assume that the scholarship is reserved for any particular racial, ethnic or cultural group.

Full-Time and Part-Time Study Options

The scholarship applies to both:

  • Full-time PhD study
  • Part-time PhD study

Applicants should check whether their intended department and research programme permit part-time study and whether the proposed research can be completed within the scholarship’s funding conditions.

Why This Scholarship Is a Strong Opportunity

The Imperial College London President’s PhD Scholarship is particularly attractive because it combines full tuition support with a substantial annual stipend and additional research-development resources.

For successful candidates, the scholarship can provide:

  • Access to a globally recognized research institution
  • Full tuition-fee funding
  • A £27,036 annual stipend at the 2027–28 rate
  • A £2,000 annual consumables fund for the first three years
  • A 3.5-year funding period
  • Access to professional development opportunities
  • Opportunities to work with leading researchers
  • Support from an academic supervisor
  • Access to Imperial’s postgraduate support services
  • Membership in a community of President’s PhD Scholars
  • Opportunities to develop research networks and transferable skills

The scholarship may be especially valuable for students who have strong academic records but require financial support to pursue doctoral research at an international institution.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

Because the scholarship is highly competitive, applicants should prepare their applications carefully.

1. Start Early

Applicants should begin the process well before the deadline.

Contacting a potential supervisor, preparing a research proposal and obtaining references can take considerable time.

2. Identify the Right Department

Applicants should select a department that closely matches their research interests and academic background.

A strong departmental fit can help demonstrate that the proposed research is realistic and appropriately supported.

3. Find a Suitable Supervisor

The proposed supervisor should have research expertise relevant to the applicant’s proposed project.

Applicants should review the supervisor’s research interests, publications, current projects and research group before making contact.

4. Develop a Focused Research Proposal

The research proposal should be clear, specific and academically compelling.

Applicants should avoid overly broad topics and should explain the problem, research questions, methodology and expected contribution in a structured manner.

5. Demonstrate Research Experience

Applicants should highlight relevant experience such as:

  • Undergraduate dissertations
  • Master’s theses
  • Research assistantships
  • Academic publications
  • Conference presentations
  • Research placements
  • Laboratory work
  • Fieldwork
  • Policy research
  • Data analysis
  • Independent research projects

6. Explain Why Imperial College London

The personal statement should clearly explain why Imperial is the appropriate institution for the applicant’s research and academic goals.

Applicants should connect their research interests to:

  • The chosen department
  • Available facilities
  • Relevant research groups
  • Potential supervisors
  • Imperial’s research environment
  • The wider contribution they hope to make

7. Choose Strong Academic Referees

Referees should know the applicant’s academic and research abilities well.

Applicants should give referees sufficient time to prepare detailed and relevant references.

8. Confirm International Eligibility

Although the scholarship has no nationality restrictions, international applicants should confirm that their qualifications meet Imperial’s requirements and that their proposed department can support international candidates.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Imperial President’s PhD Scholarship fully funded?

Yes. The scholarship provides full tuition-fee funding, an annual stipend, a consumables fund and access to professional development opportunities for up to 3.5 years.

How much is the annual stipend?

The stated stipend for 2027–28 is £27,036 per year.

How many scholarships are available?

There are 50 scholarship places available.

Can international students apply?

Yes. Applicants from around the world can apply, and there are no nationality restrictions. However, some departments may be unable to support international candidates.

Can current Imperial PhD students apply?

No. The scheme is open only to new PhD applications. Current registered Imperial PhD students are not eligible.

Is there a separate scholarship application form?

No. Applicants must apply for admission to a PhD programme through Imperial College London’s online admissions system and select the President’s PhD Scholarship option in the funding section.

Do applicants need a supervisor before applying?

Yes. Applicants must have contacted a potential Imperial academic supervisor who has agreed to supervise their proposed research project.

Can part-time PhD students apply?

Yes. The scholarship applies to both full-time and part-time study.

What is the first application deadline?

The first deadline is 2 November 2026 at 23:59 UK time.

Are there later application rounds?

Yes. Additional deadlines are:

  • 11 January 2027 at 23:59 UK time
  • 1 March 2027 at 23:59 UK time

When will successful applicants be notified?

Notification dates are:

  • 31 January 2027 for applications submitted by 2 November 2026
  • 15 April 2027 for applications submitted by 11 January 2027
  • 31 May 2027 for applications submitted by 1 March 2027

Official Contact

For questions about the application process or the PhD application form, applicants should contact the relevant Admissions department, academic department or proposed supervisor.

For questions specifically related to the President’s PhD Scholarship, applicants can contact the Student Financial Support team:

Email: student.funding@imperial.ac.uk

Applicants should also consult the official Imperial College London scholarship page and the relevant departmental admissions pages before submitting an application.

Click HERE for more information about the Imperial College London President’s PhD Scholarship.

Conclusion

The Imperial College London President’s PhD Scholarship 2027–28 is a highly competitive, fully funded doctoral scholarship designed for exceptional students with outstanding academic records and strong research potential.

The scholarship provides full tuition-fee funding, a substantial annual stipend of £27,036, a £2,000 annual consumables fund for the first three years, professional development opportunities and access to Imperial’s wider postgraduate support services. Funding is available for up to 3.5 years of PhD study.

The opportunity is open to applicants from the United Kingdom and countries worldwide, with no nationality restrictions and no stated racial or ethnic limitations. Nevertheless, candidates should confirm that their intended department can support their application, particularly if they are international applicants.

Prospective candidates should begin early by identifying a suitable PhD programme, contacting a potential supervisor, preparing a focused research proposal and gathering strong academic references.

The first application deadline is 2 November 2026 at 23:59 UK time, followed by additional deadlines on 11 January 2027 and 1 March 2027. Candidates should submit their PhD admission applications before the relevant deadline to be considered for the scholarship.

item.content:encoded:
The AJA Foundation provides philanthropic funding to organizations working to create sustainable impact in three major areas: clean water, quality education and fundamental healthcare. The Foundation funds projects globally, with particular emphasis on initiatives that address essential needs and improve opportunities for underserved communities.

Important update: The AJA Foundation’s official application page currently states that invitations for new grants are paused and applicants should check back later in 2026 for updates. Therefore, this is not currently an open grant call.

About the AJA Foundation

The AJA Foundation seeks to address unequal access to essential resources by supporting organizations working in areas it considers fundamental human rights.

Its primary focus is on:

  • Clean and sustainable water
  • Quality education
  • Fundamental healthcare

The Foundation’s approach is centered on supporting organizations that can create sustainable and measurable impact for communities that lack access to essential resources.

Areas of Funding

1. Water

The Foundation supports sustainable water initiatives, particularly projects serving rural communities in Africa.

Its water work focuses on helping communities gain access to sustainable clean-water systems and improving the long-term health, social and economic conditions associated with access to water.

2. Education

The education pillar supports organizations helping disadvantaged students overcome financial or academic barriers.

Projects can focus on improving educational access and creating opportunities for students who may otherwise face significant obstacles to achieving their educational goals.

3. Healthcare

The healthcare pillar supports organizations delivering fundamental healthcare to underserved populations, particularly in developing countries.

The Foundation’s healthcare work includes support for organizations providing essential services in communities where access to healthcare is limited.

Who Can Be Considered?

The Foundation prioritizes organizations whose missions align with its philanthropic pillars and whose programmes demonstrate potential for sustainable impact.

Projects should fall within one or more of the Foundation’s focus areas:

  • Water
  • Education
  • Healthcare

The Foundation’s geographic service area is global, meaning projects can be located in different parts of the world.

How the Application Process Works

When applications are being accepted, the process begins with a short message to the Foundation explaining how an organization’s programme aligns with one of its philanthropic pillars.

The Foundation reviews the initial inquiry and may invite an organization to submit a full grant proposal if there is sufficient alignment with its mission and funding is available.

If invited to submit a full proposal, the organization receives instructions for accessing the online application and has 60 days to complete the submission.

A full proposal may take up to six months to review before a funding decision is made.

Letters of Intent

The Foundation’s published process states that Letters of Intent are generally accepted on a rolling basis, with no fixed application deadline, and applicants can expect a response in approximately six weeks.

However, the current application page specifically states that invitations for new grants are currently paused. Prospective applicants should therefore monitor the Foundation’s official website for the next update rather than assuming that a new application can currently be submitted.

Grant Amount

There is no single fixed grant amount stated by the Foundation.

Grant sizes vary depending on the programme, and the Foundation directs applicants to its funding history for examples of previous awards.

Recent funding records show awards across the three pillars, including grants to organizations working in Uganda, Zambia, Ethiopia, Guinea, Haiti and other locations. For example, the Foundation’s 2026 funding history lists a $600,000 UNICEF water grant for Guinea, a $400,000 grant to Makolekole in Zambia, and several education and healthcare grants.

Global Funding

The AJA Foundation funds projects globally. Its funding history demonstrates support for organizations across multiple countries and regions.

The Foundation’s stated impact includes investments in water, education and healthcare initiatives designed to address fundamental needs and expand access to opportunities.

What Organizations Should Prepare

Organizations interested in applying when new grant invitations reopen should be prepared to demonstrate:

  • A clear connection to water, education or healthcare.
  • A programme capable of creating sustainable impact.
  • The community or population the project serves.
  • The development challenge being addressed.
  • How the proposed work aligns with the Foundation’s philanthropic priorities.
  • The expected impact of the project.
  • Evidence of the organization’s ability to implement the proposed programme.

Applicants should always check the official application page for the latest requirements before submitting anything.

Current Application Status

Applications for new grant invitations are currently paused.

The Foundation advises prospective applicants to check back later in 2026 for updates.

How to Apply When Applications Reopen

Organizations should visit the official AJA Foundation application page for updates and instructions:

AJA Foundation – How to Apply

Applicants should not assume that the historical rolling-LOI process means applications are currently open, because the Foundation’s current page explicitly indicates that new grant invitations are paused.

Conclusion

The AJA Foundation Grants provide potential funding opportunities for organizations working to expand access to clean water, quality education and fundamental healthcare.

The Foundation funds projects globally and has supported a wide range of organizations addressing essential needs in underserved communities. Grant sizes vary depending on the programme and previous funding records demonstrate awards ranging from smaller project grants to substantial multi-year investments. (AJA Foundation)

However, organizations interested in applying should note that new grant invitations are currently paused. Prospective applicants should monitor the official AJA Foundation website for announcements later in 2026 and use the intervening period to prepare a strong project concept aligned with one of the Foundation’s three funding pillars.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.
